summary: Private VPC upgrade failed at DB migration gate (control-plane) — migration job error, upgrade paused
description:
Issue summary
- Customer attempted Redwood Private (VPC) upgrade during scheduled maintenance window. Upgrade failed at the database migration gate for the control plane. Installer marked upgrade as FAILED and left deployment partially upgraded (control-plane pods stayed on previous version; migration job failed; gateway remained serving but admin APIs intermittently returned 503 during retries).

Impact
- Customer admin/control-plane API availability degraded during upgrade attempt (intermittent 503s). Data plane traffic continued to serve in steady state after migration job stopped retrying, but customer paused further maintenance tasks.
- Upgrade could not complete within the window; customer requested immediate rollback guidance and a safe re-attempt plan.

Customer environment
- Deployment type: Redwood Private (VPC)
- Cloud: AWS
- Region: us-east-1
- Kubernetes: EKS 1.28 (managed node groups)
- Storage class: gp3 (default), EBS CSI enabled
- DB: customer-managed Postgres in VPC (RDS PostgreSQL 14.10)
- Installer: redwood-private-installer v0.19.3
- Target upgrade: Private release 2026.01.0 (from 2025.12.2)

What happened / timeline (customer-provided)
- 22:05 ET: Ran prechecks; all green except warning on snapshot permissions (customer acknowledged).
- 22:12 ET: Started upgrade (installer upgrade apply).
- 22:18 ET: Control plane migration job started (helm hook).
- 22:19 ET: Migration job failed; installer reported failure and suggested running diagnostics bundle.
- 22:25 ET: Customer opened ticket with logs and requested rollback path.

Steps to reproduce (as executed)
1) ./redwood-private-installer upgrade plan --from 2025.12.2 --to 2026.01.0
2) ./redwood-private-installer upgrade apply --to 2026.01.0
3) Failure occurs during step: control-plane:migrations (Helm hook job)

Observed error (customer logs)
- Installer output (excerpt):
  - step=control-plane:migrations status=RUNNING
  - step=control-plane:migrations status=FAILED err="helm hook job redwood-control-plane-migrate failed: BackoffLimitExceeded"
  - hint="Collect diagnostics: ./redwood-private-installer diagnostics collect --out ./diag-2026-01-12.tgz --upgrade-correlation-id upg_01JH2T4Y0M8K5X0Z7K3V"

- Kubernetes job logs (excerpt):
  "2026-01-12T22:19:07Z" level=error msg="migration failed" err="pq: column \"downgrade_safe\" of relation \"schema_migrations_metadata\" does not exist"
  "2026-01-12T22:19:07Z" level=info msg="detected existing schema_migrations_metadata table without expected columns; refusing to continue"
  "2026-01-12T22:19:07Z" level=error msg="exit status 1"

- kubectl describe job (excerpt):
  BackoffLimitExceeded: Job has reached the specified backoff limit

Diagnostics bundle
- Customer uploaded diag tarball to secure link (SupportDrive): support://uploads/Northwind/diag-2026-01-12.tgz
- Upgrade correlation id: upg_01JH2T4Y0M8K5X0Z7K3V

Initial analysis
- Migration expects new metadata columns (introduced in the 2026.01.0 control-plane migration set) but customer’s DB appears to have an older schema_migrations_metadata table shape, likely from an older Private lineage.
- Hypothesis: customer previously ran a hotfix build or an older private release that created schema_migrations_metadata with a different schema (missing downgrade guardrail columns). The 2026.01.0 migration set is intentionally conservative and fails closed when metadata table shape is unexpected.

Workaround / mitigation provided
- Keep data plane stable: stop automated retries and avoid re-running upgrade apply until we validate DB state.
- If customer needs to restore "known good" quickly, perform rollback of chart versions (no DB changes occurred because migration job failed early).
- Rollback guidance provided per runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/private-upgrade-runbook.json (section: "Rollback after failed migration gate").

Actions taken by Redwood
- Eng/SRE reviewed diagnostics bundle and confirmed no migrations were applied (migration job failed before any ALTER statements).
- Recommended rollback path (safe) and then a supported fix: run a one-time "metadata table reconcile" job (script provided to customer) to align schema_migrations_metadata table columns with expected shape, then re-run upgrade.

Requested from customer
- Confirm whether any manual DB migration tooling was run historically.
- Provide output of: \dt and \d+ schema_migrations_metadata, plus current control-plane image tag and chart versions (installer can collect via versions report).

Resolution
- Customer executed rollback successfully (control plane and gateway back to 2025.12.2) and confirmed admin API stability.
- Next step: schedule re-attempt after we deliver patched migration preflight (better error message + auto-reconcile option) or provide explicit SQL instructions vetted by Security.

Notes
- This appears related to forward-only/downgrade metadata rollout and strict validation logic. File follow-up with Release Eng / Security to ensure installer prechecks detect legacy metadata table shapes before maintenance window.
comments:
2026-01-12 22:36 ET — Dev Patel (Support): Acknowledged. Pulling in on-call SME. Can you confirm (1) current private release version and (2) whether you’re on RDS Postgres 14.x? Please do not re-run `upgrade apply` until we review the diagnostics bundle; we want to avoid any partial state changes.

Also: please share the upgrade correlation id printed by the installer (looks like `upg_...`).

2026-01-12 22:44 ET — Customer (Northwind / Platform Eng): Confirmed: from 2025.12.2 to 2026.01.0, EKS 1.28, RDS Postgres 14.10. Correlation id: upg_01JH2T4Y0M8K5X0Z7K3V. We uploaded diag tarball to the secure upload link.

We saw intermittent 503s on the admin API during the job retries; inference traffic stayed OK. Need rollback ASAP if safe.

2026-01-12 23:02 ET — Owen Phillips (SRE): Reviewed installer logs + k8s events in the bundle. Failure is isolated to the migration hook job; control-plane deployments did not advance to new image. Good news: DB changes did NOT apply (job fails immediately on metadata column mismatch).

Rollback should be safe.

Please follow the rollback procedure in the runbook: sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/private-upgrade-runbook.json ("Rollback after failed migration gate").

High-level: `./redwood-private-installer rollback --to 2025.12.2` (or the previous known-good set in your plan output). If you used `--non-interactive` during upgrade, use `--yes --non-interactive` for rollback as well.

After rollback, please confirm:
- `kubectl -n redwood get pods` all Ready
- admin API health endpoint returns 200 for 10 mins

2026-01-12 23:20 ET — Rafael Mendes (SRE / Runbook owner): Adding details: if rollback command blocks on safety check, paste the exact error. Given migrations didn’t run, the rollback guardrails should allow chart re-apply.

If you see stuck hooks, we may need to delete the failed job before re-running rollback (runbook step 3.2).

2026-01-13 00:08 ET — Customer (Northwind / Platform Eng): Rollback completed. Admin API stable, no more 503s. We did have to delete the failed migration job to clear the hook state (per runbook). Confirmed all pods Ready.

We still want to upgrade this week. What’s the recommended fix for the metadata mismatch?

2026-01-13 00:27 ET — Owen Phillips (SRE): Root cause looks like legacy `schema_migrations_metadata` table shape. The migration runner in 2026.01.0 fails closed if expected columns are missing.

We can proceed safely with one of the following:
A) One-time reconcile: add missing columns to `schema_migrations_metadata` (no data migration of customer tables; it’s internal metadata). We’ll provide SQL + validation steps.
B) Patched build: we’re coordinating with Release Eng to add an installer precheck that detects this condition before the maintenance window and optionally runs the reconcile job.

Request: please send output of `\d+ schema_migrations_metadata` and `select * from schema_migrations_metadata limit 5;` (redact if needed).

2026-01-13 09:14 ET — Dev Patel (Support): Syncing internally with Connor O’Brien + Ethan Park on whether we can provide a supported reconcile script for this week’s window vs waiting for a patch. Tracking under INT-331 for the signing/release flow if we deliver a hotfix artifact.

In the meantime, please keep the deployment on 2025.12.2 (known good) and avoid re-attempting the upgrade until we confirm the reconcile steps.

2026-01-13 16:41 ET — Dev Patel (Support): Marking Resolved for the outage aspect (service restored via rollback). Leaving an action item for follow-up re: upgrade re-attempt plan. If you’d like, we can schedule a joint call with Solutions (Markus Klein’s team) for the next window.
resolution: Service restored by rolling back to 2025.12.2 using private rollback procedure after migration gate failure. No DB migrations applied; rollback safe once failed hook job was removed. Follow-up in progress to address legacy schema_migrations_metadata shape prior to next upgrade attempt.
internal_notes: If customer requests a hotfix build: ensure signed artifacts + provenance for private installer bundle. Consider adding precheck for legacy migration metadata table shape and more explicit remediation message. Potential linkage to downgrade guardrails work (DB migration metadata table introduction).
